text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Parliament approved the 1997 state budget, principles for drafting a new constitution, and Hungary's participation in the SFOR contingent in Bosnia on Tuesday. @
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy appointed Laszlo Kekesi as president of the tax authority effective January 1.
- Recently appointed National Police Chief Laszlo Forgacs signed a cooperation agreement in Kiev on Tuesday.

- The IMF and the government satisfactorily concluded talks yesterday regarding fulfilment of the requirements of the stand-by loan approved last March, and the government's financial and budget targets for next year.
- Industrial output in Hungary is expected to grow by 2.5 percent this year as compared to last year, said the deputy state secretary at the Ministry of Industry. @
- The chocolate and confectionery producer Stollwerck Budapest Kft is expected to close this year with sales of HUF 12 billion, up 50 per cent from last year.
- The Szegedi Paprika company has become insolvent.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- State Privatisation and Holding Co. is expected to raise the registered capital of Hungarian Investment and Development Bank by HUF 5 billion.
- The insurance company AB-Aegon expects to close this year with premium revenues of HUF 35.5 billion and profits of HUF 4 million, 30 percent up on last year's profit figure. @
- Securities investment fund management company Creditanstalt Ertekpapir Befektetesi Alapkezelo Kft is planning to launch two new investment funds.
NEPSZABADSAG
- President Arpad Goncz yesterday received Romanian senator Gyorgy Frunda, the honorary president of the Democratic Union of Hungarians in Romania.
- Hans van den Broek, the European Commissioner for foreign affairs and EU expansion, will pay a two-day official visit to Budapest beginning Thursday. @
- The Christian Democrats and the Smallholders will launch talks aimed at forging closer links within days with a meeting between two of their vice presidents.

- Hungary fell to position fifth this year in terms of attraction to foreign investors, according to a survey by the monthly Central European Economic Review. But Hungary tops the list in terms of level of integration into the global economy, financial regulations, conditions of financial investments and productivity. @
- Two kidnappings took place in Budapest last week, but as in the 15 other such incidents in the capital so far this year, neither ended successfully for the perpetrators.
- All airlines with service to Budapest raise their fares by 3 percent as of today.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- The National Bank of Hungary would close this year with losses of HUF 58.1 billion if the 1996 supplementary budget did not prescribe that the central budget pay certain central bank debts by December 31.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Intensive negotiations are going on between the Finance Ministry and the US company GE Capital regarding the repurchase of the Polgari Bank from Budapest Bank, in which GE Capital is the main strategic investor.
- The purchase contract of Magyar Hitel Bank will be signed today at the Ministry of Finance by the buyer the Dutch ABN Amro Bank, which won a closed tender.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
